default.description:
The application's own window ('main'), and every command it may call.

This is the editor, the settings panel and the agent panel, so it holds the whole declared surface except the three commands that belong to a pet window alone (`desktop_pet_close_own`, `desktop_pet_set_click_through` and `desktop_pet_host_appearance` — see `capabilities/desktop-pet.json`). Deliberately the whole of it: the boundary this file draws is the pet's, and a main window refused a command the app actually uses would be a regression dressed as a security fix. The commands are declared in `build.rs`'s app manifest; an `allow-` name that is not declared there fails the build rather than granting nothing. One of the commands here is the *only* one granted to this window and to no other, and it is worth naming for that reason: `desktop_pet_publish_host_appearance` is how the pet's windows learn the appearance this window is drawing with (§1's 「保留现有主题、强调色」). The app owns that value — it lives in this window's appearance store — and a pet window may not read the store (§7.1), so it is *published*: this window says what it is drawing, the host holds the five axes (`desktop_pet/host_appearance.rs`), and every mounted pet reads them or hears them on `pet-host-appearance`. It is a command rather than an event because §5.3 forbids an event as a config write entry point, and the ACL is what makes "only the app says what the app looks like" a fact: with this permission on `main` alone, a pet window cannot claim an appearance the user did not choose.

One of the commands it hands out is worth naming: `agent_recover_change` puts a change an agent made back, and it is the only command on this surface that writes a vault file without a tab being involved. It belongs to `main` and to no other window for two reasons — the review that offers it is drawn in the editor pane's column, and the pet window, which is the only other window in this app, holds none of the `agent_*` surface and has no vault of its own. The write itself is not this file's to bound: it goes through `VaultFiles`, so the path is confined to the root of the session the caller named, and a renderer cannot name a folder it did not open.

desktop-pet.description:
The pet's windows (§7.1) and nothing else: they may receive host events and start an operating-system drag of themselves, and they may not read a file, open a dialog, raise a notification, or move a window in any other way.

**`core:window:allow-start-dragging` is that drag, and it is the whole of it.** It is what `getWindowControls().startDragging()` needs (`platform/window.ts`), and it is what both of the pet's surfaces call: the ball through `PetFloatingBall.vue` and the character through `DesktopPetRoot.vue`, each asking the compositor once per gesture. §7.3's ban on per-frame IPC is therefore satisfied by construction rather than by discipline, and no position, geometry or monitor permission is granted to either window — a drag that needed one would not be this design, because the compositor owns the movement from the moment it starts. `desktop-pet-ball.json` names `pet-ball` and grants the same permission; it was written when the ball was the only surface that could move, and its own description says what its narrowing was for.

**Nine of the app's own commands**, one per call the pet's own page and menu make — and the ninth
is the one that answers with the *app's* appearance rather than the pet's (`desktop_pet_host_appearance`:
the theme, colour scheme, accent, contrast and body size the main window is drawing with, published by
`desktop_pet_publish_host_appearance` and held by `desktop_pet/host_appearance.rs`). It is granted here
because a pet window has to draw the same palette the app is in, and it is deliberately *not* the way
that value is written: the write is a command `main` alone holds, so a decoration can read what the app
looks like and can never say it. The direction is what §5.3's 「事件不能作为无需授权的配置写入口」
asks for, and this file is where the read half of it is stated: `desktop_pet_state` (the lifecycle's first read), `desktop_pet_set_visible` (the menu's hide), `desktop_pet_close_own` and `desktop_pet_set_click_through` (its own window, and only its own — both take the caller Tauri reports rather than a label), `desktop_pet_open_settings` (the menu's settings, which names a page and never a window), `desktop_pet_tasks` (the task feed's first read and every re-read after a push), `desktop_pet_appearance` (what the window draws, which resolves one sheet file and no directory), `desktop_pet_host_appearance` (the app's own appearance, described above), and `desktop_pet_open_task` (the bubble's click, which names a task and never a window).

Deliberately absent, and each for a reason a reader can check: every `agent_*` (a decoration does not start, stop, prompt or authorise a run), every `fs_*` (it reads no vault file), `desktop_pet_open` and `desktop_pet_disable` (creating and tearing down character windows is the settings switch's job, not a decoration's — a pet that could open more pets is a second way to reach the cap), `desktop_pet_windows` and `desktop_pet_capabilities` (the settings page's reports), `desktop_pet_read_settings`/`desktop_pet_update_settings` (writing `general.characterWindow` or `general.ball` is the switch itself, and the sizes the windows are built at ride the same write), and `desktop_pet_library`/`desktop_pet_import_character` (the character picker and the import dialog, which are the settings page's and which the pet does not need to draw the character it was already told to draw).

desktop-pet-ball.description:
The floating ball window's own boundary, one permission wide: it may start an operating-system drag of itself, and nothing else about any window.

**Why this is a second capability, and what its narrowing costs now.** It was written when the ball was the only surface that could move. `desktop-pet.json` selects its windows by `pet-*`, which the ball matches — it must, or it would hold no IPC at all — so anything added there is granted to the character windows too, and the sentence that file used to carry (the pet's windows 「may not move any window — including their own」) was true. It is not true any more: the character window has a drag of its own (`DesktopPetRoot.vue` mounts the same gesture on the sprite), and `core:window:allow-start-dragging` is in `desktop-pet.json` for `pet-*`. This file's grant is therefore a **subset** of what the pet's windows already hold rather than a widening of it, and it is kept because the union a window receives is still stated per surface: a reader asking what `pet-ball` may do finds one named window (`pet-ball`, the label `desktop_pet/ball.rs` mints) and one permission, and `command_surface_test.rs` pins both arrays exactly. Collapsing the file into `desktop-pet.json` is a change that also removes those two assertions, and it is not this one.

`core:window:allow-start-dragging` is what `getWindowControls().startDragging()` needs (`platform/window.ts`), and it is the whole of what either surface's drag calls: the compositor owns the movement once it starts, so no position, geometry or monitor permission is granted, and §7.3's ban on per-frame IPC is satisfied by construction rather than by discipline. `snap` — the reference's other half, which parked the window against an edge and persisted the position — is deliberately not wired: it needs `allow-outer-position`, `allow-current-monitor` and `allow-set-position` (three more, for a window that nothing would remember the position of across a launch), and the port declares it optional so its absence is a state the orb states rather than a permission this file can afford.
